passage: Welcome to Silver Birch Campsite. Before you set up your tents, I'd like to run through a few essential rules. The site is divided into three zones: the family zone, the quiet zone, and the group zone, and you'll each be assigned a pitch number when you check in. Quiet hours run from ten p.m. to seven a.m., and this is strictly enforced in the quiet zone, though the group zone allows a little more noise until midnight. Campfires were originally allowed anywhere on the grass, but after a small incident last summer, they're now only permitted in the designated fire pits near the washroom block. Firewood can be purchased at reception for four pounds a bag. Showers and toilets are located at the washroom block, which is open twenty-four hours, and hot water is available until eleven p.m. each night. Dogs are welcome in the family and group zones but must stay on a lead. If you need to extend your stay, please let reception know by nine a.m. on your final day, as pitches are often booked in advance. Finally, please make sure all rubbish is placed in the bins near the entrance, not left at your pitch.
stem: What is the main purpose of this talk?
explain_zh: 這段獨白是營地管理員在遊客搭帳篷前說明營地的各項規定，屬於典型的規則說明。其餘選項如販售裝備、關閉營地都沒有出現。

passage: Hello everyone, and welcome to the new Energy and Motion exhibit here at the Science Discovery Museum. I'm Harriet, and I'll be showing you around. This exhibit opened last week and covers everything from simple machines to renewable energy. We'll start with the giant pendulum in the main hall, which demonstrates the conservation of energy — you can even trigger it yourself by pulling the lever every fifteen minutes. Next, we'll move to the wind turbine model, where visitors can adjust the blade angle and see how it affects power output. The interactive robotics zone was originally going to be open to all ages, but because some of the equipment involves small moving parts, it's now restricted to visitors aged eight and above. After that, we'll visit the solar energy station, which includes a real solar panel connected to a screen showing live energy readings. The whole exhibit tour takes about fifty minutes, and there's a hands-on workshop at the end where kids can build a small model car. Please remember that food and drinks aren't allowed inside the exhibit hall, though there's a cafe just outside.

To explain how to become a museum member

passage: Good morning, and welcome to today's Old Town walking tour. I'm Desmond, and I'll be leading you through the historic centre. We'll begin at the clock tower, which was built in 1742 and is one of the oldest structures still standing in the city. From there, we'll walk along Merchant Street, known for its preserved medieval shopfronts, before reaching the old market square. The tour was originally planned to include a stop at the riverside gardens, but since they're closed for renovation this week, we'll instead visit the covered arcade, which has some beautiful nineteenth-century architecture. Along the way, I'll point out a few hidden details, like the carved stone faces above some of the doorways, which locals believe were meant to ward off bad luck. The full tour covers about two and a half kilometres and takes roughly ninety minutes at a relaxed pace. Please wear comfortable shoes, as some of the streets are cobbled and uneven. We'll take a short break halfway through at a small square with public benches. Feel free to ask questions at any point — I'm happy to pause the group.

options: To sell tickets for a concert
To lead a historic walking tour

passage: Good afternoon and welcome to Hillside Zoo. I'm Fatima, and I'll be guiding today's tour. We'll start at the primate enclosure, home to our family of chimpanzees, before heading over to the big cats section, where you can see our two Sumatran tigers. Feeding time for the tigers was originally scheduled for two p.m., but because one of the keepers is running a special talk this afternoon, feeding has been pushed back to three thirty instead. After the big cats, we'll walk through the aviary, home to more than eighty species of birds, including several that are part of an international breeding programme. Our newest arrival, a baby giraffe born just three weeks ago, can be seen in the savannah enclosure, though she's still quite shy around large crowds. Please keep noise to a minimum near her enclosure. The full tour lasts about eighty minutes, and there's a cafe near the exit for anyone who'd like a snack afterwards. Flash photography is not allowed near the nocturnal animal house, as it can disturb the animals' sleep cycles. Restrooms are located next to the gift shop at the main entrance.

passage: Hi everyone, welcome to the Riverside Art Centre. I'm Nadia, and I'll be introducing today's pottery workshop before we get started. This session usually lasts two hours, but since we have a larger group today, we'll extend it to two and a half hours so everyone gets enough time at the wheel. All materials, including clay and glazes, are included in the workshop fee, so you don't need to bring anything except an apron if you have one — we do have spares if not. We'll begin with a short demonstration on the pottery wheel, followed by hands-on practice where each of you will make your own small bowl. Finished pieces need to be fired in the kiln, which takes about a week, so you won't be able to take your bowl home today — instead, we'll contact you when it's ready for collection. The centre also runs painting and sculpture workshops on other days, and members get a twenty percent discount on all future sessions. If you'd like to continue with pottery, we offer a six-week beginner course starting next month. Please switch off your phones during the demonstration, and feel free to ask questions once we begin practising.

passage:
A: Dr. Farah, we've collected our survey data, but we're not sure which statistical test to use.
B: What exactly are you comparing?
C: We want to see if there's a difference in study hours between students who work part-time and those who don't.
A: We initially planned to use a simple t-test since we only have two groups, but our sample sizes are quite different, around forty and one hundred and twenty.
B: In that case, a standard t-test might not be the most reliable choice. I'd recommend running a Mann-Whitney U test instead, since it handles unequal group sizes and doesn't assume a normal distribution.
C: That makes sense, our data did look a bit skewed when we plotted it.
A: Should we still report the means, or just the medians?
B: Since the data is skewed, report the medians, they'll give a more accurate picture than the means in this case.
C: Got it. Should we come back after running the test to check our interpretation?
B: Yes, let's meet again next Monday afternoon so I can review your results before you write them up.
stem: What are the students mainly seeking help with?
